scenes.narration: Move this dot anywhere inside the triangle. The three distances change, but their total refuses to move. These are perpendicular distances to the sides. And this triangle has three equal sides. Try pushing the dot toward a corner. One distance grows while the others shrink. Why should they balance perfectly? Join the dot to all three corners. We have divided the same big triangle into three smaller ones, with no gaps and no overlaps. Each little triangle uses one full side of the original as its base. Those three bases are equal. Now rotate the pieces so their bases face the same way. Their heights are exactly the three distances we were measuring. A triangle's area is half its base times its height. Because the bases match, adding these areas is the same as adding the heights, then multiplying by half the common base. But together the pieces still have the area of our original triangle. So their heights must add to the big triangle's height. Watch the dot move again. The colored distances trade length, while the total stays fixed. At the very top corner, two distances shrink to zero and the third becomes the full height. That extreme case was hiding the answer all along.
